ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the inverting input terminal of the operational amplifier is labeled “-”, the input signal u_i is connected to the inverting input node through the resistor R; the capacitor C is fed back from the output terminal to this inverting input node; the non-inverting input terminal is labeled “+”, and is grounded through R+; the output terminal is labeled u_o. Therefore this is an inverting integrator circuit. Reasoning calculation: The problem gives u_i=-1 V, R=10 kΩ, C=100 μF, the power supply voltage is ±5 V, and asks for u_o at t=3 s. The integration time constant RC=(10 kΩ)(100 μF)=10000×100×10^-6=1 s. According to zero initial output u_o(0)=0, the inverting integrator output is u_o(t)=-(1/RC)∫_0^t u_i dt. Substituting u_i=-1 V and RC=1 s gives u_o(t)=-∫_0^t(-1)dt=t V. Therefore at t=3 s the ideal output is +3 V. Since +3 V is within the ±5 V power supply range, the operational amplifier is not saturated, so the output is 3 V.
